To destroy the world that abandoned her, she must first pretend to save it.

In a realm fractured by privilege and the raw pulse of Aura, the powerful thrive in the glowing sanctuaries of the Safe realm protected by the elite Neonshield Agency while the forgotten rot in the shadows. But a silent, cosmic terror is stirring, the Warwillers, shapeshifting horrors that feed on fear, have begun their invasion. Their greatest weapon isn’t a monster; it’s Kiramay.

Born in the desolation of the Ruined Unsafe Zone, Kiramay is a survivor fueled by a lifetime of betrayal. Recruited by the very horrors she should fear, she is sent into the heart of Neonshield as a Trojan Horse. To aid her, she is bound to "The Becoming"—a cursed system that grants immense power, but only in exchange for cold-blooded betrayal. Wearing the mask of a brilliant new hero, Kiramay infiltrates the last line of defense, poised to tear down the civilization that cast her aside. But as she delves deeper into the rot at the core of the city, the lines between ally and enemy begin to blur.

In a game where leveling up requires breaking hearts and burning bridges, Kiramay faces a final, devastating choice: Will she be the savior the world doesn't deserve, or the devil that finally ends it all?

The protocol is set. The mask is on. Let the world learn to fear her name.

I can't leave my apartment.

Not won't. Can't.

Four days ago the world broke. Something they are calling the Fracture. The sky split for about eleven seconds and when it closed again, the streets had monsters on them and the news anchors were dead on a loop. My phone still works. Nobody is answering.

On day two, a blue box appeared in my living room and told me I had been assigned a class. Hearthbound. It sounded cozy. It isn't.

The rules are simple.

I bleed, I claim. Four milliliters per square meter. Once my blood dries on a floor, that floor is mine. Inside my claim I am basically a small god. Outside it, the air itself shoves me back the second I try to step through my own front door.

So here is my problem.

My apartment is forty four square meters. My sister lives on floor three. My parents are two buildings over. My neighbors are dying behind drywall I can hear through. The whole city is ending. And the one place I am allowed to stand is the one place I swore, four years ago, that I would never leave again.

I guess I am going to have to grow the apartment.

One inch at a time.


What to expect:

- First person. Tired narrator. Dry humor. No screaming, no speeches, no chosen one monologues.

- Shut in MC who physically cannot step outside his claimed territory. Hard rule, not a quirk. The whole volume one is written from inside his own walls.

- Kingdom building from a studio apartment up. Room by room. Floor by floor. Building by building.

- A System called the Warden Ledger that sounds like a sarcastic HOA manager and might hate me a little.

- Blood cost progression. Every meter is paid for in real ml. The numbers go on the page.

- A Golden Finger that only works inside your own walls. Outside, you are just a guy with a cut on his hand.

- One love interest. Slow burn. No harem. She fights outside. I hold the inside.

- A sister I owe an apology to. Neighbors who become subjects. A cat who may or may not be reading my status screen over my shoulder.

- Post apocalyptic setting. Small scale at first. Then not.

- Chapter length 2200 to 2800 words. Royal Road standard.

- Daily updates when I can manage it. Milestone bonus chapters on follower counts.

- Long form serial. First volume is 52 chapters. Settle in.


Content notes: graphic violence, some profanity, on page self inflicted blood cost for the magic system, no sexual content.


Some people run toward the fight.

I just locked the door, drew a line in my own blood, and waited for the world to knock.

Before the System arrived, pulling millions of people into its cruel games, Kiwi was only a pet raven living with her loving owners.

Before she became a raven, she had been a human, a cat, and maybe she had been a fish at some point, but all those memories were vague and blurry to Kiwi the raven. After the System descended, everything changed. She now remembered things about her human past that she never wanted to know, memories that Kiwi could not even spend time grappling with, because she also found herself forced into a series of horrifying games where death became an actual concern.

Also, everything Kiwi went through would be televised to the violence-hungry 'audiences' throughout the galaxy, and she barely even got a cut of the profit!

"What can that weak looking thing do?" The audience laughed when Kiwi first appeared, "Being pretty won't save you."

The bloodthirsty viewers stayed, betting on when Kiwi would finally die, but the only thing that died was their internet connection from the unprecedented high number of beings watching her stream. Or rather, cheating the System and breaking the game.

That's right. If she can't win the game, she'll just destroy it. After that, she might finally find out what truly happened to her a lifetime ago.

Didn't you know? Ravens are known for how smart they are.

Note: Kiwi would stay in her human form more than half of the time. However, her bird form would evolve into something stronger eventually.

What to Expect

- MC who becomes smarter as the story goes on

- A focus on using intelligence to solve problems

- MC building a team that works together

- A System that sends our characters to different worlds to go through Quests and trials <<< Infinite Flow inspired

- Female x Male romance eventually

What not to Expect

- A strong focus on stats

- Using brute force to go through the quests (most of the time)

- Harems

Hints of there being another dimension have been rumored for hundreds of years. But is it true? The government has been known to keep secrets —Too many in fact. Yet the world has continued to spin up until the year 2050.

Many reports have been made of people in hospitals disappearing. Graveyard visitors. Funeral homes, prisons, battlefields. The only connection these places have is they have intense emotional resonance. Coincidence?

Earth has come up with several issues but one strikes the most, overpopulation. Thousands of death-row inmates have been sentenced to death in three weeks, but the government had other plans.

Sullen, a death-row sentenced to death in three weeks. His hope was lost until an interview had suspended his death. Introducing a new program, Program Shade, where all of his crimes would be pardoned if he signed a contract. With no other information given, he had no option.

Signing himself into mystery, he soon would be another person who “disappeared”. Tossed in deadly magical trials filled with never seen creatures, will Sullen survive and take his ticket to obtain freedom?

For Ren Kurogane, death was never the beginning of a new life.

Even less did he dream of awakening in another world with the ability to summon a giant black scythe and a single skill etched into his soul.

In the labyrinthine city of Eretis, the gods gather adventurers in their respective households and bestow blessings upon them to explore Tartarus, the vast dungeon beneath the city.

Ren, too, dreamed of becoming an adventurer.

However, there was one problem.

No god could bestow a blessing upon him.

His soul already belonged to an authority even the gods could not comprehend.

After being rejected countless times, Ren finally met Eresh, the beautiful goddess of death. Her household was on the verge of collapse.

She had no money,

no followers,

and her temple was crumbling.

And the roof probably wouldn't survive the coming winter.

Upon learning of the new goddess's circumstances, Ren makes a very simple decision:

To venture into Tartarus, complete quests, and earn enough money to provide her with a decent home.

His world isn’t being invaded.

It’s being evicted.

When portals open across Kavareth, Desmond Rask discovers the truth buried in the fine print: his entire reality is under an expired lease agreement, and the Interdimensional Housing Authority (IHA) has arrived to repossess it.

Desmond isn’t a hero. He’s a contract-obsessed nobody with an unhealthy talent for finding loopholes. Unfortunately, the loophole he finds requires seven candidates to survive a lethal System trial series.

Even more unfortunately, the IHA gets to choose the candidates.

So they choose the worst possible people for the job.

Now Desmond has to survive trials meant for actual champions, when instead he's got:
-A failed influencer.
-A grumpy plumber.
-A scheming criminal.
-A hippe-dippie pacifist.
-A retired interdimensional monstrosity.
-And one HEAVILY armed canine. 

The System expects heroes.

The landlords expect failure.

Desmond and his crew don't expect to live past breakfast.

Ryo thought moderating online drama was the worst part of his job. 

After years of night shifts, caffeine, and defending the Internet's most polarizing figure — Llewellyn, the world's most famous hero, the System's golden boy, and the only person alive with Transcendent-level Elemental Mastery — Ryo figured he'd seen it all. Conspiracy theories? Fan petitions? Cult-like followers? All in a night's work. 

What he didn't expect was the System deciding his online arguments counted as combat experience and dropping him into a magical apocalypse with Llewellyn himself! He also didn't expect the Internet to start shipping them!

And he certainly didn't expect the System's idea of "combat partner" to involve an absurd amount of physical contact disguised as Healing Bonuses, shared body heat, Dungeon environments that look like dates, or being randomly teleported onto Llewellyn's lap!

Llewellyn might be the strongest person on Earth, but he has no one to watch his back. Luckily for him, Ryo has had to deal with his unhinged online following for years… and he is more than willing to get his hands dirty in person.

this is a personal project I'm just writing when I can. it is in essence for my son to read one day I just don't mind people reading it. this story is inspired by Dante's Inferno, modern system fantasy, and Greek epics but in modern Appalachia 

Elmore is a family man at heart just living his life in the mountains of WV. Raised a hillbilly who had aspirations but chose a happy slow life over childhood dreams. He has a son with his wife. They are as happy as the American dream can offer. He is smart and resourceful, a jack of all trades formed from a life of struggle. He has built a life that is anything but struggle.

Eventually the world comes to a crisis. Things happening that make no sense and people freaking out left and right. As a hillbilly he survives and his son is none the wiser. Even with his isolation and survival skills he is faced with a desperate world and an act of heroism brings those survivors that haven't left for the cities under his care. 

When a hillbilly is given power all he can do is his best. But the world refuses to let him rest and after being the one to be attacked too many times he finally makes a change to help the world in the best way he can.

But a man's life is not forever and the modern world is not the only place or time he will defend. You must ask yourself the meaning of life when death is common and birth is just as ubiquitous. If memories fade and pain dulls, what comes of you if those memories never leave you, no matter how much atrocious events you witness. This is his destiny.

When the Milky Way collided with the rogue galaxy Claytrone, Earth did not receive a savior. It received a death sentence. 

Dimensional rifts tore the world apart, vomiting mythical alien refugees and terrifying cosmic beasts onto our soil. Civilization crumbled, replaced by a cold, bare-bones System UI. It offered no cheat skills, no shops, and no mercy—it was merely a silent mirror reflecting raw statistics. Earth had transformed into a hardcore, old-school MMORPG where a single death meant losing weeks of agonizing grinding. 

In this brutal new era, Nox Welbert awakened the most despised profession: **[Blacksmith]**. 

With no combat skills, no support magic, and zero funding, Nox is deemed dead weight. Rejected by every raiding party and exiled from the safe zones, his choice is clear: adapt or starve. But a blacksmith cannot survive inside dungeons. To live, Nox must hunt alone in the forbidden ruins of the old world. 

Armed only with heavy, hand-forged steel traps, his own body as bait, and a deep understanding of metallurgy, Nox begins his solo grind. While others rely on flashy magic, Nox manipulates the brutal laws of weight limits, thermal shock, and weapon durability. 

They thought a blacksmith belonged in the workshop. Nox will show them that with the right equipment and a flawless strategy, even the gods can be fractured. 

**What to expect:** 

Hardcore Old-School MMORPG Mechanics: Strictly enforced weight limits (encumbered debuffs), punishing death penalties (EXP loss), true grinding, and a cold, minimal System UI.

Smart & Tactical MC: No overpowered cheat skills. The MC survives through trap-crafting, kiting, and professional blacksmithing logic (Thermal Fracture/Armor Melting).

Dark Fantasy / System Apocalypse Grid: A gritty, realistic survival atmosphere where every stat point matters.

Would you accept power that makes you nearly unstoppable, but turns you into a monster? What if the strength you always dreamed of began to consume you from within? 

If you want to discover the power that will allow you to survive, then keep reading.

He just wanted to live in peace, but his enemies brought him war. Now, he will make all those who hurt him pay. In Apocalypse Berserker, the isekai hero isn’t destined to save humanity… he’s meant to end it.

Molten lost everything in a single night. Invaders from the world of Duniya slaughtered his parents, and the woman he loved.

Marked by a mysterious system, he’s dragged into Duniya itself: the very world that took everything from him. There, life becomes a brutal game where every choice matters and every fight could be his last. Leveling up isn’t optional anymore. It’s the only way to survive.

Through the system, Molten becomes something never seen before: a fire Berserker: the first of his kind. A weapon powerful enough to destroy the invaders. A chance to finally claim his revenge… if he lives long enough.

Because in Duniya, Berserkers are feared above all else. They are engines of destruction driven by rage, and consumed by madness.

Nearly impossible to kill, for whatever doesn’t destroy a Berserker only makes them stronger. That’s why they’re hunted. That’s why they’re feared.

And now, with the rise of a fire Berserker… the apocalypse in Duniya draws closer.

But Molten’s power comes at a cost.

Every skill erodes his mind. Every victory feeds something darker within him. And when the fury takes over, he can no longer tell friend from enemy.

The stronger he becomes, the clearer his fate: to lose himself completely… and become something without mercy, without control. But… if you want to survive to exact revenge, is there any alternative other than becoming a monster?

Molten isn’t being trained to save the world. He’s being forged into the weapon that will end it.

Inside Apocalypse Berserker, you’ll find:

 High-stakes combat where every decision can mean life or death.

A clear, addictive LitRPG progression fantasy system: level up, unlock skills, evolve.

A protagonist who grows stronger… and more dangerous.

An isekai story.

Elemental powers that combine for devastating reactions in battle.

Classic RPG classes: Berserker, Paladin, Hunter, Mage, and Shielder—each with unique strengths and weaknesses.

Powerful armor with striking designs that enhance your abilities.

Real strategy: enemies with mechanics, patterns, and exploitable weaknesses.

A world in crisis where nothing is as it seems.

A mysterious system hiding more than it reveals.

Alliances, betrayals, and fights where trust can get you killed.

Epic moments that keep you turning pages.
